tob-10229: The writings of Zhuangzi, China’s great Taoist storyteller, turn philosophy into fable and joke. He tells of a man who dreams he is a butterfly, a giant fish that becomes a bird, and sages who laugh at the world’s certainties — all to loosen the mind’s grip on fixed ideas. Herbert Giles’s translation captures the wit of this second pillar of Taoism alongside the Tao Te Ching.
tob-10829: Blavatsky wrote The Key to Theosophy as a plain question-and-answer introduction to her movement. In it she explains karma, reincarnation, and the Theosophical view of God and the soul in everyday language. Intended for newcomers put off by the denser Secret Doctrine, it remains the clearest doorway into Theosophical thought.
tob-4029: Adam Smith’s Wealth of Nations founded modern economics with a plain claim: when each person chases their own gain, open contest can serve all — the ‘unseen hand.’ His study of work, markets, and trade knocked down the old closed-shop order. Out in 1776, it remains the bible of free-market thought.
tob-4129: Mead’s Faith Forgotten limns the Gnostic schools — Valentinians, Basil’s men, and the rest — from strewn old witnesses. His brief bright studies woke English minds to the lost Christianities. The old heretics live again in his pages. The book stays the classic English door to Gnosis.
cia-0000115229: An untitled November 1945 document on the statement of Viacheslav Ivanovich Toropovsky — a fuller name for the S. Toropovsky of the October statement. The files circle the same man from different angles. The entry shows how fragmentary records slowly resolve into a person.
cia-0000118929: A November 1985 document on CIA secrecy agreements — the legal promises that bind everyone who handles classified information. Signing one means prison if you talk. The entry is refreshingly honest about the paperwork of secrecy: the intelligence world runs on signed oaths.
cia-0000119729: A September 1956 forecast that Hungary's domestic policies were about to be overhauled. Reformers were pressing for change from inside the communist system. The document catches the pre-revolutionary mood — the sense that something had to give, weeks before Budapest exploded.
cia-0000124329: A July 1953 report on the status of an American plane crew downed in the Swatow area of China. The war was ending, but the accounting was just beginning. The entry is one crew's story — the search for answers that families waited decades to receive.

plos-pone-0000029: A 2006 PLOS ONE study on the critical role of methylglyoxal and AGE in mycobacteria-induced macrophage responses — the truncated title cuts off the rest. Toxic sugar byproducts shape how immune cells fight TB bacteria. The paper is the role: the byproducts, critical.

un-sc-res-829: Security Council Resolution 829, adopted in 1993 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
guazzo-compendium-maleficarum-1929: Francesco Maria Guazzo's Compendium Maleficarum in Montague Summers's 1929 translation — the 1608 witch-hunter's manual, a lurid handbook for finding, trying, and burning witches. Guazzo's credulous zeal makes it a chilling window into the witch craze. The book is the manual: the witch-hunt, instructed.

frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d129: The president's secretary Early to the secretaries of State, War — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 129. The White House staff wrote the cabinet. The memo is the staffwork: Early, coordinating.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d229: A memorandum by the United States Chiefs of Staff, November 18, 1943 — Document 229. A third. The memo is the tripling: the papers, many.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d329: The President to the Secretary of State, November 26, 1943 — Document 329. The White House wrote the department. The message is the direction: the president, instructing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d429: The president's special assistant Hopkins to the ambassador to the Soviet Union — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 429. The insider wrote Moscow's envoy. The cable is the insider's: Hopkins, to Harriman.
formation-of-the-union-1750-1829: Albert Bushnell Hart traces how scattered colonies grew into one nation, from the 1750s through the Revolution, the Constitution, and the early republic. Written with a scholar's care and a storyteller's pace, the book shows the forging of the United States. A firm base for all later study of the young republic.
arxiv-2605-09129: Finding the circuits inside a language model by hand is slow; finding them from data is the dream. Daking Rai and Mor Geva pursue data-driven circuit discovery for interpretability, automating the hunt for the model's inner machinery. The 2026 paper turns interpretability from craft into method.
arxiv-2605-09329: Speculative execution — guessing ahead and checking — speeds up chips; doing it at test time could speed up models. Avinash Kumar, Sujay Sanghavi, and Poulami Das explore test-time speculation. The 2026 paper bets that guessing ahead pays off handsomely in inference.
arxiv-2605-09429: Vision-language models sometimes go blind to obvious image content — a strange visual aphasia. Jie Ma, Yihang Liu, Zhike Qiu, and colleagues evade it with contrastive adaptive semantic token pruning, cutting tokens without cutting sight. The 2026 paper keeps VLMs seeing clearly by pruning wisely.
arxiv-2605-09529: Layered materials conduct heat and electricity differently depending on how the layers stack. Zhongjuan Han, Wu Xiong, Zhonghao Xia, and colleagues compute stacking-dependent thermoelectric transport in Sc2Si2Te6 from first principles. The 2026 paper is materials physics for waste-heat harvesting.
arxiv-2605-09829: The early universe holds too many UV-bright galaxies — and dust may explain the surprising excess. D. Burgarella, V. Buat, A.K. Inoue, and colleagues propose a dust-origin transition at redshift beyond 9. The 2026 paper is cosmic-dawn astrophysics with stardust.
plos-pone-0003429: HIV researchers tracked the virus adapting to human immunity in this 2008 paper. The killer T-cell response forces HIV to mutate its way around each person's HLA immune fingerprint, and the team studied how subtypes B and F of HIV-1 converge under that pressure. Mapping these escape patterns helps vaccine designers predict where the virus will dodge next.
plos-pone-0003529: Cancer researchers traced how a virus protein rewires cell chemistry in this 2008 paper. The HPV16 E7 oncoprotein pushes cells toward cancer partly by activating NHE1, a pump that makes the cell interior alkaline. The team mapped the chain, PKA to RhoA to blocked p38alpha, showing how one viral protein tilts the cell's entire chemical balance.
plos-pone-0003629: Cancer biologists Jin Yoon, Phelps, and Bush found a tether that keeps tumors home in this 2008 paper. ICAM-2 links the cell membrane to the actin skeleton, and its expression marked a nonmetastatic, better-prognosis phenotype. The membrane-actin link emerges as a natural brake on the wandering that makes cancer lethal.
plos-pone-0003729: In 2008, Stover, Fidzani, and Molomo took stock of Botswana's AIDS fight. Using clinic records, surveys, and program data, they estimated past HIV trends and measured what treatment and prevention programs had achieved. The report card shows a nation turning the tide against one of the world's worst epidemics.
plos-pone-0003829: Back in 2008, a group asked why Salmonella strains pick different victims. Comparing pathogenicity islands across serovars, they found genes evolving at different speeds, with host range written in that divergence. The analysis links the pace of gene change to which animals each strain can sicken.
plos-pone-0003929: In 2008, Wang, Mouraux, and Liang caught the brain over-answering rapid sounds. When tones came less than 400 milliseconds apart, the auditory N1 wave grew instead of shrinking. The paradoxical boost defies the usual habituation to repeated stimuli. The finding rewrites what the N1 brain wave is really measuring.
plos-pone-0004029: In 2008, a team blocked two tiny RNAs to slow prostate tumors in mice. Shutting down miR-221 and miR-222 impaired the growth of prostate carcinoma grafts. The two microRNAs are overactive in several human cancers, acting as oncogenes. Silencing them offers a new angle against hard-to-treat prostate cancer.
plos-pone-0004129: In 2009, Zhang and Lin chased a missing piece of dinoflagellate messages. They retrieved the spliced leader sequence used in dinoflagellate mRNA processing. The short 22-letter tag starts many of their genes. The neat find fills a gap in plankton genetics.
plos-pone-0004229: In 2009, Cui and Loraine audited gene-chip redundancy. They checked whether repeat probes on Affymetrix chips agreed. The overlapping probes mostly agreed with each other. The audit guides cleaner microarray analysis. The careful work helps labs trust chip results more.
plos-pone-0004329: In 2009, Ilin and Richter-Levin found play healing young rat trauma. Enriched environments reversed learning and mood damage from juvenile stress. Playful housing overcame the early harm fully. The finding supports enrichment as therapy. The rat work echoes childhood trauma research.
plos-pone-0358129: Fear of movement can lock in back pain long after tissues heal. This study protocol laid out sensor-based measurement of fear avoidance and movement patterns in healthy people with mechanically induced lower back pain. The planned measurements will show precisely how fear reshapes the way people move.
plos-pone-0358329: Factories need to spot surface defects with barely any training examples to learn from. FH-Net uses frequency-domain and hierarchical dual enhancement for few-shot defect segmentation. The method learns from just a handful of samples — practical, deployable AI for the production line.
plos-pone-0358429: Autistic women face unique barriers in pregnancy care — sensory overload, communication gaps, dismissed concerns. This Brazilian qualitative study used the hermeneutic-dialectic circle to surface communication barriers in perinatal care for autistic women. Their voices point toward maternity care that actually fits them.
plos-pone-0358229: What makes ice-and-snow tourists happy? This big-data analysis explored the antecedents of tourist satisfaction at winter destinations. The data-driven findings tell resort managers what visitors actually value — beyond the powder — from food and lodging to lift lines and atmosphere.
plos-pone-0357829: When blood flow returns to a starved limb, the reperfusion itself injures tissue. This rat study showed N-acetylcysteine — a well-known antioxidant — attenuates oxidative-stress-driven cell death and collagen deposition after hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion injury. The compound emerges as a practical tissue protector for surgical and trauma care.
plos-pone-0329429: Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi — plants’ ancient underground partners — vary enormously across landscapes. This Ethiopian study found spore density and species diversity differ within plant species and between dry Afromontane forests in the northwest. The patterns guide conservation of these invisible allies.
plos-pone-0355829: Predicting forest fire risk demands both fuel data and climate data, fused intelligently. This physically aligned deep learning framework couples fuel and climate multivariate factors for fire risk prediction. The model forecasts where fires are likely to ignite — with physics guiding the AI.
plos-pone-0357029: Vitamin D supplement use varies widely across Egypt and Jordan — and the reasons matter. This survey-based study measured use patterns and their associated factors in both countries. The findings guide smarter supplementation campaigns where deficiency is common.
plos-pone-0356529: Washington’s Cosmic Crisp apples sometimes develop mysterious green spots. This paper showed that changes in skin properties are a consequence — not the cause — of the green spot disorder in ‘WA 38’ apples. Ruling out the obvious suspect redirects the search for the true culprit.
plos-pone-0348529: Common daisies hide Fibonacci mathematics in their ray flowers — but the numbers vary. This paper examined variations in ray flower numbers of Bellis perennis, revealing the hidden cues of Fibonacci order. The findings show nature’s mathematics is messier — and more interesting — than textbook spirals.
plos-pone-0355229: Middle adolescents making health decisions need tools, not lectures. This paper developed an intervention for 15–17 year olds using the Behaviour Change Wheel to empower their decision-making about health. The theory-driven design respects teenagers’ autonomy while steering them toward healthier choices.
plos-pone-0352129: Fear of missing out drives Dhaka’s university students toward compulsive phone use — with mental health costs. This cross-sectional study tested FOMO as a predictor of smartphone addiction and mental health outcomes. The findings map a distinctly modern affliction — and point to where interventions might break the cycle.
plos-pone-0355729: Predicting gestational diabetes could combine clinical data with genetics in one AI. This paper built a hybrid mamba-transformer architecture fusing clinical and genetic features for the task. The fused model promises earlier, more accurate identification of pregnancies at risk — enabling timely intervention.
plos-pone-0354729: South Korean public hospital nurses burn out at alarming rates. This paper examined the associated factors through the Job Demands–Resources lens. The findings reveal which demands drain nurses and which resources protect them — a blueprint for hospital reforms that keep caregivers caring.
plos-pone-0349429: Drug trafficking in Dhaka follows patterns that were never systematically mapped. This paper unveiled the patterns and sociodemographic characteristics of trafficking in the Bangladeshi capital. The findings give law enforcement and public health an evidence base beyond anecdote.
europmc-pmc2821929: Stem cells from mouse bone marrow can calm angry immune cells, this 2010 paper reports. The authors show mesenchymal stromal cells turn activated macrophages toward a regulatory-like profile, dialing down their aggression. The finding supports using these stem cells to treat inflammatory disease. It also reveals how the two cell types talk to each other.
europmc-pmc2855329: Brewing more of a wanted chemical in germs means picking the right gene tweaks. This 2010 paper brings OptForce, a math search for every tweak set that hits output goals. The authors demo the search. The tool turned strain design from art to calculation.
europmc-pmc2871929: Sperm production runs on stem cells, and this 2010 review explains their rulebook. The authors cover spermatogonial stem cell regulation and spermatogenesis. Their overview gathers how the testis keeps making sperm for decades. The review is a primer on male fertility biology.
europmc-pmc2882429: Needle-therapy trials need clear write-ups to be judged fairly. This 2010 paper brings revised STRICTA rules for reporting acupuncture trials, building on CONSORT. The authors' checklist wants detail on needles, points, and the healer's craft. Their rules lifted a murky field toward openness.
europmc-pmc2893129: Knowing where a plant protein works means knowing its address in the cell. This 2010 paper presents Plant-mPLoc, a top-down method for guessing plant protein locations. The authors' approach lifts accuracy over older tools. Their program helps botanists place proteins where they belong.
europmc-pmc2904929: Friendly gut germs might trim cholesterol, and this 2010 review weighs the claim. The authors survey cholesterol-lowering effects of probiotics and prebiotics from lab and animal studies. Their weighing finds promise with caveats. The review tempers probiotic hype with evidence.
europmc-pmc2909929: Polycystic ovary syndrome touches mood, fertility, and body chemistry across a lifetime. This 2010 review covers the many faces of PCOS, from teen years to later life. The authors span mind, cycles, and metabolism. Their guide aids care for millions of women.
europmc-pmc2916829: A bacterium living in insects can block West Nile virus. This 2010 paper shows native Wolbachia endosymbionts of fruit flies and Culex mosquitoes boost host resistance to West Nile infection. The authors' finding extends Wolbachia's shield. Their work hints at broad antiviral uses.
europmc-pmc2936529: Bacterial genomes favor certain DNA letters, and this paper asks whether selection drives the tilt. The authors test for selection on GC-content across bacterial genomes. Their analysis separates true selection from random drift. Their work tackles a classic genome puzzle.
europmc-pmc2940729: The malaria parasite's shape-shifting surface protein hides in gene diversity. This 2010 paper maps PfEMP1 variety across seven parasite genomes. The authors' divide-and-conquer analysis tames the variation. Their work aids vaccines against a moving target. Each genome revealed new variants to catalog.
europmc-pmc3036629: Repaired blue-baby hearts need MRI watch. This 2011 review shows how heart MRI tracks fixed tetralogy of Fallot and times valve swaps. The author guides heart doctors. Their overview shapes care. Leaky valves get spotted before they fail. Kids dodge repeat open-heart surgery longer.
europmc-pmc3046429: Blood microRNAs may track breast cancer. This 2010 paper tests tiny blood RNAs as markers for early and spread breast cancer. The authors' data shows promise. Their work points to liquid biopsies. A blood draw beats a biopsy for comfort. The test could slot into routine checkups.
europmc-pmc3078329: A messenger protein drives gut inflammation. This 2010 paper shows interleukin-23 fires up gut inflammation through T cells. The authors reveal the driver. Their work points to biologic drugs. Blocking it calms Crohn's disease. The drugs are now clinic staples. Newer blockers refine the approach.
europmc-pmc6517429: Stopping bleeding from a torn artery or a wounded heart is brutally hard: blood pressure pries loose most glues, and tissues are wet and moving. Scientists designed a light-activated hydrogel that bonds strongly even to slick, beating surfaces. In animal tests it sealed arterial and cardiac wounds fast. The material could one day help surgeons and medics control bleeding that current products cannot.
europmc-pmc6522529: Most air purifiers trap particles but do nothing to kill germs caught in the filter. Researchers coated filters with metal-organic frameworks - ultra-porous crystal sponges - that destroy bacteria on contact when lit. The photocatalytic coating adds germ-killing power to ordinary filtration, pointing toward air cleaners that both capture and neutralize airborne microbes.
europmc-pmc6539529: Injecting bacterial toxin (LPS) into animals sparks brain inflammation that mimics early neurodegeneration - a useful laboratory stand-in. This review explains how the LPS model bridges acute neuroinflammation and chronic diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. By studying the bridge, researchers can test anti-inflammatory strategies before the slow human diseases take hold.
europmc-pmc6560329: Knowing how much of a patient is fat versus muscle guides nutrition care - and two tools dominate: bioelectrical impedance (a painless electric pulse) and DXA scans. This review compares BIA and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry for measuring body composition in health and disease, weighing accuracy, cost, and practicality.
europmc-pmc6572829: Cancer drugs stop working as tumors evolve resistance - combinations could outflank them, but testing every pair is impossible. In a community challenge, teams built algorithms to predict winning drug pairs from tumor genomic data. The assessment reveals which computational approaches actually forecast effective combinations for individual patients.
europmc-pmc6604129: Can exercise protect the minds of people with Alzheimer's? Pooling trials in a meta-analysis, researchers found physical activity linked to better cognitive function in patients. The effect is modest but real - another reason movement belongs in dementia care plans, alongside whatever drugs can offer.
europmc-pmc6629629: Head and neck cancers are aggressive, genetically tangled, and hard to treat - surgery and radiation remain the mainstays. This clinical update surveys the molecular biology driving these tumors and the challenges ahead: why targeted drugs lag and where research is pushing. A state-of-the-field guide for a tough cancer group.
europmc-pmc6651129: SIRT1 is a longevity-linked enzyme that moonlights in genome defense. This review covers its double duty in cancer: guarding DNA repair and epigenetic stability, while sometimes aiding tumors. The sirtuin sits at a crossroads of aging and malignancy - a tantalizing but tricky drug target.
europmc-pmc6688129: Tumors recruit fibroblasts - structural cells - and corrupt them into immune-suppressing henchmen. This review exposes cancer-associated fibroblasts as mediators of immunosuppression: shielding tumors, remodeling tissue, feeding growth. The dark side of the stroma may be immunotherapy's missing target.
europmc-pmc6692429: NF-kB is inflammation's master switch - but what is it doing inside mitochondria, the cell's power plants? This review gathers the scattered evidence on NF-kB's mitochondrial cameo: a familiar protein in an unfamiliar place. The cameo may link immunity, energy, and disease in unexpected ways.
europmc-pmc6747329: Everyone 'knows' metastases cause 90% of cancer deaths - but nobody checked. Using population data from a Norwegian cancer registry, this study measured what share of deaths metastases truly cause. The myth-busting result resets one of oncology's most quoted statistics.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-29: Published in 2007 by the Government Accountability Office, this report examines safety on airport runways and ramp areas. It reviews leadership gaps, technology shortfalls, and other challenges that contribute to accidents and near-misses where aircraft operate on the ground. The report calls for sustained effort across agencies to reduce runway incursions and ground collisions, and it grades the federal response to a long-standing aviation safety problem.
gao-gaoreports-b-299929: A second 2007 GAO ruling for AlliedBarton Security Services LLC — three more contract fights, same year, same firm. The guard company kept challenging federal awards, and GAO kept the calls coming. Read with its twin ruling, the pair maps how the government buys guard work — and how hard the big firms fight for it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1129: A reactor-building boom was brewing in 2007, and GAO checked whether the atom referees were ready. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission's licensing gears and staffing mostly passed, GAO found — but big unknowns hung over the coming flood of plant bids. The report tests the safety watchdog on the eve of its busiest stretch in decades.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-629: The IRS's own audit report card came due in 2007 — GAO's letter tracks the financial audit and the fixes still owed. The findings keep the tax agency's books under a watchful eye. The letter's premise: the collector must itself be beyond reproach.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-729: Foreign airports got American report cards in 2007 — GAO's report says overseas assessments and carrier inspections lifted security, but the watch needed work. The findings balance credit and caution. The report's reach: the sky has no borders, so neither should the screening.
openalex-w7204279629: Maps can be acts of resistance. This article tells how the riverside community of Curupere Grande in Para mapped its own territory through social cartography, recording land, livelihood, and memory. The authors describe the project born from a geotechnology course. A vivid account of a traditional community drawing its own lines.
openalex-w7119516229: Potassium ions drift through water in ways that matter for batteries and biology. This paper studies their diffusion with pulsed-field gradient NMR, a magnetic technique that tracks molecular motion. The authors tackle the method's limits for these fast ions. A physical-chemistry study of salt on the move.
openalex-w7204785729: Glass that turns blue light into ultraviolet could serve sensors and sterilizers. This paper reports praseodymium-doped silica glasses, melted while levitating, emitting strong UV under blue excitation. The authors pushed past normal doping limits. A photonics study of glass that upgrades light.
pmc-13439629: In this 2026 study, people with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome who followed a healthy lifestyle had lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. The syndrome bundles heart, kidney, and metabolic risks, and the two-cohort analysis shows lifestyle still moves the needle. It is encouraging evidence for prevention in a high-risk group.
pmc-13351929: A 2026 biophysics paper combining cell-free protein synthesis with single-molecule rotation assays for high-throughput mutational analysis of F1-ATPase — the rotary motor that makes cellular energy. Watching individual motors turn reveals how mutations change the machine. The integrated pipeline is the technical advance.
pmc-13421129: This 2026 Pan American Health Organization paper assessed El Niño in the Americas for 2026–2027 — public health risks and preparedness priorities. The climate phenomenon threatens health across the hemisphere. The paper sets the preparedness agenda.
pmc-13422929: This 2026 systematic review synthesized qualitative evidence on clinicians' and patients' views of virtual hospital care. Hospital-at-home needs both sides' buy-in. The review captures the experiences.
pmc-13470029: In this 2026 paper, space radiation impaired long-term endothelial integrity and may promote atherosclerosis in ApoE-deficient mice. The cosmic rays damaged vessels. The finding matters for deep space travel.
pmc-13458029: In this 2026 systematic review (the title is truncated), behavioral economics-informed interventions' impact on the STI care cascade was synthesized. The nudge strategies were evaluated. The review is the evidence map.

pmc-13428229: A 2026 PET/CT paper detecting Borrelia-triggered seronegative rheumatoid arthritis using gallium-68 DOTA-Siglec-9 imaging (the title is truncated). The Lyme-triggered arthritis was visualized. The detection is the diagnostic advance.
pmc-13419929: A 2026 paper on DU-Vigilance — capturing unsuspected problems in drug utilization. The surveillance system caught the unexpected. The vigilance is the safety net.
pmc-13376729: A 2026 paper, "The Wells-Riley Model Revisited II," addressing parameter uncertainty and population heterogeneity in the airborne infection model. The classic model's limits were probed. The revisiting refines infection risk estimates.
pmc-13414529: In this 2026 post hoc analysis of RCTs, ulcerative colitis therapy efficacy and safety did not differ by age. The age-independence is reassuring. The analysis supports treating older patients fully.
pmc-13514729: This 2026 animal nutrition paper showed dietary energy-protein balance regulated slaughter traits, meat quality, digestive enzymes, and fecal microbiota in early-weaned gray-feathered geese (the title is truncated). The feed balance shaped the meat. The regulating is the finding.
pmc-13527129: A 2026 battery paper on the moisture-induced surface degradation mechanism of argyrodite Li6PS5Cl under dry-room conditions. The solid electrolyte's Achilles' heel was mapped. The mechanism informs manufacturing.
pmc-13483529: A 2026 paper identifying IL1RN, MUC1, and SERPINA1 as key NET-related biomarkers in ulcerative colitis-associated intestinal fibrosis via bioinformatics and experimental validation (the title is truncated). The fibrosis biomarkers were found. The identification is the advance.
pmc-13473129: A 2026 soil science paper on dynamics of soil organic carbon under wheat cultivation in saline soil of the Yellow River Delta. The salty soil's carbon was tracked. The dynamics inform management.
pmc-13472929: This 2026 paper introduced DTOFW — a lightweight tri-branch time-frequency fusion network for video-based recognition of diarrhea-related calf behavior. The AI watched the calves. The network serves farm health.
pmc-13451929: In this 2026 taxonomic paper, the congrid eel genus Gnathophis in Taiwan was revised, with three new species described. The eels were formally named. The descriptions are the taxonomy.
pmc-13517829: A 2026 paper on genetic and environmental causes of aggression in the domestic cat. The feline temper's roots were studied. The causes inform behavior.
pmc-13463229: In this 2026 paper, inter-assay variability in anti-JC virus serology was examined in the era of natalizumab biosimilars — implications for PML risk stratification. The test variability threatened risk assessment. The implications demand standardization.
pmc-13424529: A 2026 nasopharyngeal carcinoma paper: naringin sensitized the cancer cells to paclitaxel by inducing AKR1C3 expression. The citrus flavonoid boosted the chemo. The sensitizing is the combination mechanism.
pmc-13556229: This 2026 virology paper found a small viral protein suppressed immune amplification by two distinct mechanisms. The viral immune evasion was decoded. The suppressing is the pathogenesis insight.
arxiv-2606-16229: Program analyzers use "abstract transformers" to reason about what code can do without running it. This paper shows how to automatically synthesize the best such transformers using parallel bit-vector optimization — searching many possibilities at once.
